security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the mseccfg CSR MML bit (Machine Mode Lockdown) is specified as a sticky bit that, once set to 1, cannot be cleared to 0 until a full PMP reset (hart reset). If the CSR write logic in the Chisel/Verilog mseccfg module allows software to write 0 to the MML field via a CSRRS/CSRRW instruction after MML has been set, this constitutes a spec violation. The hardware must implement a per-bit interlock: when mseccfg.MML transitions from 0→1, the write-enable for the MML bit must be permanently gated off (hardwired to ignore further writes) until the reset signal is asserted. This requires a sticky state flop (e.g., RegInit(0.B) with conditional write gating) in the CSR register file that latches the 'locked' condition, preventing any subsequent CSR write from clearing MML. Similarly, the MMWP (Machine-Mode Allowlist Policy) bit has the same sticky-once-set semantics and requires identical hardware write-gating. If the XiangShan CSR module treats these as ordinary WARL bits without the sticky interlock, M-mode software can disable Smepmp protections at any time, defeating the entire hardware-enforced isolation between M-mode and lower privilege levels.
security_spec.summary: mseccfg.MML and MMWP sticky bits require hardware write gating that permanently blocks clearing after set; if CSR module treats them as ordinary WARL fields, M-mode code can disable Smepmp protections at runtime, defeating hardware-enforced M-mode confinement
